This decision prioritizes the stability of the university's academic infrastructure over the recreational streaming needs of the student body, even though the service is legal and widely used.", "summary": "Oxford University banned Spotify to protect academic network bandwidth from peer-to-peer congestion."}, "1": {"original": "Oxford University banned Spotify to prevent network slowdowns caused by peer-to-", "rephrased": "The University of Oxford has implemented a ban on the peer-to-peer music service Spotify, citing the high bandwidth demands of its decentralized data-sharing architecture as the primary reason for the restriction. This policy aims to preserve sufficient network capacity for essential academic activities, acknowledging that the service's technical design creates a strain on the university's digital resources that outweighs the benefits of free music access for students.", "summary": "Oxford University banned Spotify to prevent network slowdowns caused by peer-to-peer data sharing."}, "2": {"original": "The university provides free internet access for students because it's an educa", "rephrased": "The institution provides free internet access to students specifically as an educational resource, establishing a clear boundary where recreational usage is permitted only if it does not compromise network performance. Consequently, the university argues that while students may use the connection for leisure, this freedom is conditional upon the traffic not consuming enough bandwidth to slow down the system for others, thereby balancing student rights with the technical limitations of the shared infrastructure.", "summary": "The university allows recreational internet use only if it does not slow down the network for others."}, "3": {"original": "Bandwidth usage scales up significantly with thousands of users, making recrea", "rephrased": "The Computer Services department explains that while individual recreational bandwidth usage might seem negligible, the cumulative effect of thousands of users simultaneously accessing services like Spotify creates a massive strain on the university's network infrastructure. This scaling issue means that justifying a network upgrade based on such recreational traffic is technically unfeasible, especially when compared to the massive data requirements of genuine academic research projects.", "summary": "OUCS argues that scaled-up recreational bandwidth use strains infrastructure more than academic needs."}}
